Every row of this page is a line of `internal/features` in spin, and a test there resolves it against the tree. A row that says **built** names what shows the feature exists - a procedure the control plane serves, a command the CLI has, or a test - and, under **End to end**, the tests that drive a real runner and its guest and check what the feature did, or what no test checks yet. spin's build checks that each of those tests is there and not quarantined; whether it checks the whole feature is its review's. A row that says **not built** is an item of [`docs/ROADMAP.md`](https://github.com/spin-stack/spin/blob/77380b13da641c24e3f79b9c7586c39888f4e7ba/docs/ROADMAP.md). The page is written by `task reference` from `spin features` at spin `77380b13d`, and cannot say a feature the binary does not.

## Partly there

Nothing today.

## Not built

Each is an item of `docs/ROADMAP.md`, with the command that checks it.

- **What a workspace grew to is asked for and never recorded** (Workspaces)
- **Placement cannot be told which kind of host a workspace belongs on** (Workspaces)
- **A workspace whose host never comes back is moved only when little would be lost** (Administration)
- **Nothing that needs a kernel runs in CI** (Platform)
- **`spin/v1` is still ignored by the breaking-change gate** (Platform)

## Limits

Not planned: a limit of the platform or of where it runs today. [Limitations](/overview/limitations/) says what each means.

- **AWS only** (Platform): The Terraform module is the one supported install; nothing else is packaged or tested.
- **x86-64 only** (Platform): Runners are x86-64 machines with nested virtualization.
- **The CLI runs on Linux x86-64 and macOS Apple silicon** (Platform)
- **One region, one control plane** (Platform): A machine that fails is replaced in minutes, not seconds.
- **No GPUs** (Workspaces): There is no way to ask for a runner of a particular kind.
- **Linux guests only** (Workspaces): Booted with the kernel spin provides.
- **No IPv6 inside a workspace** (Network)
- **TCP only for published ports** (Network)
- **A diff does not see everything** (Snapshots): A file is hashed only when its size, inode or times changed; extended attributes are not compared.
- **A memory snapshot resumes only on the same machine** (Snapshots): The same QEMU, guest kernel and guest init; a disk restore has no such limit.
- **Disk chains have a limit** (Snapshots): At the limit the top layer grows instead, so less of the recent work is in the bucket.
- **Work since the last upload can be lost** (Snapshots): A runner uploads writes in layers, on the RPO, on snapshot and on stop; what it had not uploaded goes with it.
- **No multi-factor authentication of Spinbox's own** (Access): Sign in through a provider that enforces it.
- **No invitations** (Access): A person signs in once before they can be added to a team.
- **Team roles are fixed** (Access): Owner, admin and member.
- **Nothing pages anyone** (Observability): Metrics, logs and traces stay inside the installation; there are no alerts.
- **An update is one way** (Administration): A release older than the one that last started the database refuses to start on it.
